scenario: HMDP seckill orders are accepted by the web JVM but remain pending while the separate Kafka consumer JVM is stopped.

injection_method.action: Stop only the isolated hmdp-consumer JVM after one baseline order commits; keep hmdp-web, MySQL, Redis, and Kafka running.
guardrails: Use dedicated one-partition main/retry/DLT topics and consumer groups.
Use only AIOPS_P22_ tagged vouchers and distinct local test accounts.
Send orders through POST /voucher-order/seckill/{voucherId}, never directly to Kafka.
Do not stop containers, delete data, or create an Incident manually.

healthy_baseline: Consumer group has at least one active member.
Committed offset exists and lag is zero.
The baseline HTTP-accepted order exists in tb_voucher_order.
fault_window: HTTP accepts additional seckill orders and Kafka topic end offset increases.
Consumer group member_count is zero and lag is greater than the demo threshold.
tb_voucher_order count for the test voucher stays unchanged until consumer recovery.
recovery: Consumer group regains a member and lag drains to zero.
Previously pending test orders appear in tb_voucher_order.

expected_root_cause: Kafka consumer JVM unavailable; web continues producing, so order messages accumulate before MySQL persistence.

expected_hypothesis.description: Kafka consumer unavailability causes seckill order creation delay.
counterexamples_to_check: Kafka broker unavailable or producer send failed.
Consumer members healthy with lag zero.

expected_evidence: get_kafka_status returns success for the dedicated topic and group.
member_count=0 and committed/end offsets show positive lag for consecutive windows.
HTTP acceptance and test-voucher MySQL count divergence are externally verified.
optional_evidence: search_application_logs only after the dual-JVM log path is supported by the existing allowlist.
